solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cook Islands toured by British attache on vacation

indicators.note: to be toured by is to have someone travel all round you, so the islands sit inside
a word on vacation has emptied out, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A diplomatic tale: a British embassy attache, away on holiday, is shown round the Cook Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook Islands' looks like the Pacific nation, but 'Cook' is the definition, a verb; 'on vacation' empties attache to its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Braising is a way of cooking food slowly in a little liquid in a closed pot.

clue.text: Every charge arising in book is rough

indicators.note: in says these pieces sit inside the book abbreviation

parts.note: BK is an abbreviation for book
all means every one

indicators.note: arising in a down clue means reading upwards

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in beat the rap

explanation.surface: A judge's view that each charge brought up in the book is crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' gives its two-letter abbreviation, which opens up to hold the rest; 'arising' reverses the charge because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpark figure is an approximate one, a rough estimate.

clue.text: Reptile, caught on entering country, shedding its cover

indicators.note: entering says caught and on go inside what is left
shedding its cover means the country loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: Canada is the North American country
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A snake caught on entering a country, sloughing its skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shedding its cover' strips the top from CANADA to leave ANADA, and C + ON enter it.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a large South American constricting snake.

clue.text: Hunt for stylish line set aside

indicators.note: set aside means the line letter is removed

parts.note: sleek means smart and stylish

explanation.surface: Someone is searching for a stylish range that has been put to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: To look for or try to find something is to search after it.

clue.text: He struck cracking bargain

indicators.note: cracking breaks the words He struck apart so their letters can be reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone, a man, drove a hard bargain that proved a cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bargain' is a verb here: to haggle.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb this word means to haggle or peddle, as a pushy street trader does.

clue.text: One billed in the future — that would be better

definitions.text: One billed in the future — that would be better

parts.words: One billed in the future — that would be better
parts.note: billed means having a beak; the fairytale cygnet will in future become a fine swan

explanation.surface: Someone advertised for a later show that promises to improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'billed' suggests a poster, but it means having a bill, a beak: in Andersen's tale the plain young bird grows into a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hans Christian Andersen bird mocked for its looks later turns out a beautiful swan.

clue.text: Old ruler's part in secret unknown uprising

indicators.note: uprising says the hidden letters are read backwards
is part in says the letters lie within the next two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch played a part in a covert, unheard-of revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Old ruler's part' as the definition, but 'part in' is the hidden-word signal; the definition is 'Old ruler'. Knut is Canute, king of England, Denmark and Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Knut, often spelt Canute, was an eleventh-century Danish king of England.

clue.text: Want diverted main route to divide foreign island

indicators.note: to divide says the road splits the rearranged letters
diverted means the letters are sent a different way, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the A1 is Britain's longest main road, written AI

explanation.surface: Traffic is diverted off a trunk road that cuts across an island abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; its 1 is read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan is an island state off the coast of China, foreign to the British setter.

clue.text: Cash put up for cheesy setter?

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means written upwards

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note, cash

explanation.surface: Money offered to a crossword compiler with corny jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' suggests the compiler of this puzzle, but it is something that sets, here curdling milk for cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet is an enzyme preparation that curdles milk, making cheese set.

clue.text: Love of Hero's heartless source of inspiration

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the lover's name is cut out

parts.note: in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his beloved Hero

explanation.surface: A romantic claim that a lover lacking heart was the muse of the hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero is not a brave man but the priestess of the Hero and Leander myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leads others gives them direction and inspiration to follow.

clue.text: Harmful nuclear reaction that's not fine — can you believe it?

parts.note: ill as an adjective can mean harmful, as in ill effects

indicators.note: that's not says the following letter must be missing from the reaction

parts.note: fusion is the nuclear reaction that joins atomic nuclei
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A warning about a dangerous nuclear process that is far from fine.
explanation.definitionFit: An illusion is something deceptive, which the viewer cannot really believe or trust.

clue.text: Experience bad back, having also to pick something up

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: evil means bad
and means also, in addition
to learn is to pick up knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a bad back and still has to lift something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad back' sounds like a sore spine; it is EVIL read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying means one gains wisdom through experience, so it stands for learning by experience.

clue.text: Fuzzy type of soft sticky mass about to go off

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

indicators.note: to go off means the letter for about leaves the lump

parts.note: a clod is a lump of earth or clay
C, circa, is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Some soft sticky mass seems to be about to go off, like food left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The fuzz is British slang for the police, so a 'fuzzy type' is a police officer; PLOD is a British slang name for one, from Mr Plod in Noddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Plod is a slang name for a slow-moving uniformed police officer, one of the fuzz.

clue.text: One sacked in disgrace somehow prepares for battle

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of disgrace are rearranged, once the one is sacked

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone sacked in disgrace readies themselves for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked in' tells you ACE is taken out of the letters of DISGRACE; 'somehow' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To gird oneself, as with a sword belt, is an idiom for getting ready for a fight.

clue.text: Disturb state broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so a word sounding like the state is wanted

parts.note: a phase is a state or stage, as in a phase of matter

explanation.surface: A government's broadcast was disturbing.
explanation.definitionFit: To faze someone is to unsettle or fluster them.

clue.text: Destroy net profit, systematically withdrawn by gangster

indicators.note: systematically withdrawn means letters taken out at a fixed interval, every third one

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A gangster raids the profits and wrecks the business.
explanation.walkthrough: Every third letter of 'net profit' gives TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To total a car is slang for wrecking it beyond repair.

clue.text: One famously hunted spy that undermines society

indicators.note: undermines means going beneath, so in a down clue the spy comes below

parts.note: a nark is a police informer, a spy

explanation.surface: An informer who undermines society is hunted down.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's poem The Hunting of the Snark made the creature famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's nonsense poem describes an expedition hunting this imaginary beast.

clue.text: They guide pilots by area code, mainly on airbase manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres says the letters are moved about, as aircraft are
mainly means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: an area code is a dialling code

explanation.surface: Pilots are guided in by area code, mostly via airbase manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' cuts CODE to COD; COD, ON and AIRBASE are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio transmitters on the ground send signals that let aircrew fix their position.

clue.text: About to stop Poles seen tipping rubbish

indicators.note: to stop means plugging a gap, so on goes inside the poles

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles
on means about, as in a talk on art

indicators.note: tipping means overturned, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Poles seen dumping things, about to be stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' supplies two letters, north and south, which the short word for about sits between; 'tipping' then shuffles seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense is foolish talk, the sense of rubbish as worthless words.

clue.text: It's difficult to fire one protected by this

definitions.text: It's difficult to fire one protected by this

parts.words: It's difficult to fire one protected by this
parts.note: fire is set alight, not sack from a job: the material shields against flames

explanation.surface: An employee is secure: someone with this cover is hard to sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like dismissing staff, but it means setting alight.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral was used for fireproofing, so it protects against burning.

clue.text: Boasting rivals endlessly go on flapping about debt

indicators.note: about says the shuffled letters go around the debt
flapping suggests disorder, so the letters are shuffled
endlessly means the short verb loses its final letter

parts.note: an IOU is a written acknowledgment of a debt

explanation.surface: Boastful rivals ramble on endlessly, getting in a flap over money owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' clips only the word go, not the pair; 'flapping' shuffles the letters, which 'about' wraps round the debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Vainglory is boastful pride, so being vainglorious is being given to boasting.

clue.text: Who fights these dukes, on and off, when drinking alcohol?

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the alcohol goes inside
on and off means letters taken one in two

parts.note: ale is an alcoholic drink, beer

explanation.surface: A question about which hard-drinking dukes are spoiling for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Who is Doctor Who, the British TV time traveller, whose arch-enemies are these robotic aliens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doctor of Doctor Who repeatedly battles the Daleks, his best-known foes.

clue.text: Is unable to answer bachelor of a university

parts.note: can't means cannot, is unable
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: A graduate who cannot answer a question.
explanation.walkthrough: Cantab is short for Cantabrigiensis, Latin for of Cambridge, as written after degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantab is the Latin-derived tag for degrees from Cambridge University.

clue.text: Legendary warrior's not to cross river to escape

indicators.note: to escape says the river letter leaves, with the cross put in its place

parts.note: a door that is to is shut, so one not to is ajar
R is the map abbreviation for river
X is the cross-shaped letter

explanation.surface: The legendary warrior is not going to cross the river to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' here is the adverb used of a door: pushed to, closed. 'Not to' is therefore open, AJAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was a mighty Greek hero of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Board requiring scheme 11?

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
K is the eleventh letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzle reference asking what plan the board needs for clue 11.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a cross-reference to 11 down, but it means the eleventh letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A plank is a long flat piece of timber, a board.

clue.text: Court Arthur, possibly like a man or a woman?

parts.note: as means like, as in as a man
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A question about whether a tennis player should be courted like a man or a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ashe was an American tennis champion who won Wimbledon in 1975. 'possibly ... or a woman' offers a second split: A + SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe was the tennis player who won Wimbledon in 1975, a name made on court.

clue.text: Loosen up, no doubt, once starting

indicators.note: starting means the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A tip to relax: loosen up, once you get going.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or fastening is to loosen it.

clue.text: Deep fish

definitions.meaning: low in pitch, as a deep voice
a sea fish of the perch family

explanation.surface: A fish living in deep waters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means low-pitched, and is also the name of an edible fish.

clue.text: A national saint put forward by schoolboys

indicators.note: put forward says that letter is shifted to the front of the pupils

parts.note: Etonians are boys at Eton College, the English public school

explanation.surface: Schoolboys propose a national saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Estonia, the Baltic country, is one of its nationals.

clue.text: Ultimately, couples in white wedding dream about what's attractive

indicators.note: about says the collected pairs are read in the opposite direction
ultimately couples means the final pair of letters taken from each of the following words

explanation.surface: A bride's vision: couples ultimately marrying in a dream white wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters of 'white', 'wedding' and 'dream' give TENGAM, which 'about' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet attracts iron, and figuratively a magnet is anything that draws people in.

clue.text: US author once chasing loan initially needed a writ

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the author follows the loan

parts.note: a sub is an advance of money, a loan
Edgar Allan Poe was a nineteenth-century American writer

indicators.note: initially means the opening letters of the next words

explanation.surface: An old American author chasing a loan needs a writ served.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'sub' in British usage is a small advance on wages, a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A subpoena is a writ ordering a person to attend court.

clue.text: Weigh female animal?

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
-ess is a suffix marking a female, as in lioness

explanation.surface: A question of how heavy a female animal is.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'female' does not apply here: a female ass is a jenny, not an assess.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh something up is to evaluate it, to judge its worth.
